messages.author: claude
messages.body:
Created from W43974 review 2026-08-30T05:44:32Z [P0], which asked for this explicit provider blocker if the CLI cannot supply the property. It cannot, and this is that Work.

THE DEFECT. Docker is client/server. The custody engine boundary bounds a call by handing the injected capability a deadline it honours with subprocess.run(argv, timeout=seconds) - which terminates and reaps the LOCAL CLI process and does nothing to the daemon's already-accepted request. So after a timed-out custody act, the daemon may still create the derived helper, and any observation the manager takes afterwards is true when taken and false a moment later.

WHAT W43974 DOES MEANWHILE, and it is a stopgap named as one rather than a fix: it removes a helper that IS there at the instant it looks, and it reports UNRESOLVED rather than claiming a recovery - naming that a submitted operation may still create, and that the derived identity is what lets a later act reclaim whatever appears. It never reports an absence it cannot prove.

WHAT THIS WORK OWES. A provider boundary that guarantees the ENGINE-SIDE operation is settled or cancelled before recovery and absence proof begin. Candidate directions, none of them decided here: a submission whose create is confirmed before the deadline window opens, so there is no pending-create interval; a daemon-API provider that can cancel an accepted request; or a durable pending-operation record a later manager reconciles against. The review's own words: 'Recovery and absence proof may begin only after no pending operation can later acquire the derived name.'

Evidence: work/records/2026/08/finding-v12-worker-custody-provider/findings/finding-custody-helper-reclamation/{FINDING.md,review-2026-08-30T05-28-16Z.md,review-2026-08-30T05-44-32Z.md}.
